text:
Alex: Heads-up — I'm opening a thread to track the proposed decommission of session-gateway and moving the minimal responsibilities into request-garden + tenant-sidecar. Wanted to collect tradeoffs and an incremental plan.
Maria: Nice. Can you summarize current ownership and why we want to split?
Alex: session-gateway handles: sticky session mapping, legacy token translation, per-tenant rate bucketing, and a small in-memory cache for hot prefixes. It's drifted into routing, auth glue, and short-term KV.
TJ: TL;DR: it's a maintenance hotspot. Hard to test, high blast radius, and blocks per-tenant rollout work.
Nora: Agree. The runtime team also sees it as a barrier to better hot-path optimizations. But what's our compatibility story for tokens and sticky affinity?
Alex: Proposal sketch: 1) Move sticky affinity into request-garden (hotpath router optimized for latency). 2) Move token translation to tenant-sidecar (per-tenant transformation/checkout). 3) Keep a small compatibility proxy shim for 6 months to intercept legacy clients.
Samir: Sounds reasonable. Concern: request-garden runs in the hotpath — adding logic could increase p99. Need strict microbenchmarks.
Maria: Could we extract a tiny C++ affinity lib used by both request-garden and the shim to avoid duplication?
TJ: Yes — single impl for determinism. Then request-garden uses native lib, shim links to it.
Nora: DB ownership question: session-gateway currently writes sticky records to redis-census. Do we let request-garden own writes or make a fronting write service?
Alex: Idea: read-path for affinity stays local (in-process LRU with KV-cache), writes go to a new "affinity-writer" service that batches to redis-census asynchronously. That reduces hotpath jitter.
Samir: Async writes are fine but need eventual-consistency tolerances documented — we can't break some of the teardown semantics we rely on today.
Maria: Also: telemetry. We need per-tenant counters moved along so billing and quota still line up.
Alex: Yep — add a migration step: copy current counters to centralized quota-store and add a dual-write for 2 weeks.
TJ: Rollout plan (sketch):
- Phase 0: Feature flag + read-only shim. Clients experience unchanged behavior.
- Phase 1: Deploy affinity lib -> request-garden reads only, shim still authoritative. Microbench and perf tests (2 weeks).
- Phase 2: Introduce affinity-writer (canary to low-traffic tenants). Start async-write + reconciliation job.
- Phase 3: Tenant-sidecar starts handling token translation for opt-in tenants.
- Phase 4: Flip shim to passive, run observability for 1 month, then retire session-gateway.
Nora: Who will own the reconciliation job? SRE or platform?
Samir: Platform should own reconciliation logic; SRE will add runbooks for failure modes. OpsBot: Reminder: create incident runbook stub when affinity-writer reaches canary stage (link: https://internal/runbooks/affinity-writer).
Maria: Need a compatibility test harness to simulate legacy clients and edge timing. I can pair with Eng QA to produce a small load script and validation checks.
TJ: Perf targets: request-garden p50 must remain within current p50-2ms, p99 increase < 7ms. We'll add strict alerts if breached.
Alex: Config snippet for the feature flag rollout (example):
```yaml
feature_flags:
  session_gw_decom_v1:
    enabled_for_percentage: 0
    monitor: session_gw_decom.metrics
    safe_thresholds:
      p99_latency_ms: 20
      error_rate_pct: 0.5
```
Nora: Good. Also list of acceptance criteria before we cut the shim: metrics stable, reconciliation error < 0.1%, quota parity verified, and no client-side token failures in last 72h.
Samir: Ops notes: plan a rollback path where shim can be re-enabled quickly and affinity-writer quiesced. Add a toggle to make writes synchronous for rollback windows.
Maria: Security: tenant-sidecar will need scoped KMS access for token translation. Security team sign-off required before opt-in begins.
Alex: I'll assemble an RFC doc with these phases + timelines and rough owner assignments. Asking folks: volunteer owners?
TJ: I'll own performance verification and the benchmarks.
Nora: I'll take reconciliation + acceptance tests with QA.
Samir: I'll be platform owner for affinity-writer and ops runbooks.
Maria: I'll lead the compatibility harness + coordinate security review.
Alex: Thanks — I'll post the RFC link shortly and tag owners. Quick wins: create the shared affinity lib repo and a branch for the shim to link to.
TJ: One more ask — can we define a clear latency budget for each tenant tier during canary? We should codify it in the rollout description.
Alex: Agreed. Add that to RFC.
Maria: :thumbsup:
OpsBot: Deploy bot triggered: session-gateway decomp tracker created (#DC-2139).
Alex: Cool — RFC coming, will ping again.
Maria: Thanks everyone.
